correctness.rationale: For each exponent pair, the formal ordered-sequence generating series equals 1/(1-t(A-1)), A=((1-x)(1-y))^-1. A rational bivariate binomial identity yields P=t(1+t)^(M-1) Jacobi_m^(0,M-m)(1+2t). Endpoint nonvanishing and classical Jacobi orthogonality give all stated roots and multiplicities. Normalizing by P(1) gives the product of finite Bernoulli probability generating factors. The sum variance is at least (M-1)/4, which diverges for a+b→∞; boundedness verifies Lindeberg. A standalone independent-recursion checker passed all 144 exponent pairs 1..12 but is not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Prior art already defines the divisor-function polynomial for all integers and supplies every individual factor-length coefficient; Kinder gives a Jacobi evaluation only for the total. The asserted novel target is the variable-length Jacobi identity, all-root census and its exact fixed-integer independent-Bernoulli/Gaussian law. Inspection of closest full-text sections and targeted searches revealed no direct covering implication. Historical identities or generic real-rootedness theorems might provide an implicit alternative derivation; originality is qualified, not independently certified.

value.rationale: A natural random variable is the number of factors of a uniformly selected ordered factorization. Previous divisor-function papers compute coefficients or totals; the exact two-prime Jacobi reduction reveals every zero and a finite independent Bernoulli decomposition. It also yields a Gaussian law for arbitrary diverging exponent pairs at fixed prime support, which differs from known averaged-over-integers central limit theorems. This is structural arithmetic information rather than a small table or a routine numerical improvement.
